tagline: From Mohawk River canal locks to Adirondack lakes and lumbering remains
intro: Southern Adirondack Trail connects Herkimer and Little Falls on the Erie Canal with Speculator, passing mountains, lakes and Adirondack hamlets. New York’s scenic-byway program gives the route a length of 112 miles and identifies scenic and recreational themes. The Adirondack Regional Tourism Council highlights canal history and the lakes at Piseco, Pleasant and Speculator, with a loop encircling Piseco Lake. Hiking, boating, cycling and fishing are available along the trail, while the tourism council describes the lakes as destinations for camping and fishing.

Water shaped travel here before the scenic route. At Little Falls, rapids obstructed upstream passage, and the need to carry goods past the falls encouraged trade. The Erie Canal, completed in 1825, improved transport through the valley. Farther into the mountains, Nobleboro preserves remains of a pulpwood boom and mill; at Lake Pleasant, lumber companies floated logs down the Sacandaga River to Glens Falls.

Begin with Herkimer and Little Falls, then head toward Newport on West Canada Creek. Continue through Nobleboro and Hoffmeister toward Higgins Bay on Piseco Lake’s southern shore. After the Piseco loop, the route reaches Speculator, where Routes 8 and 30 meet beside the northeastern end of Lake Pleasant. At Speculator, the namesake mountain rises south of the village and can be seen from most of it.

moments.title: Little Falls
moments.text: The Mohawk drops 45 feet in less than a mile at Little Falls, passing through a narrow rocky gap. Those rapids once impeded upstream travel; carrying goods past them helped establish a trading place. The Erie Canal changed that passage when it was completed in 1825, linking the Great Lakes with the Hudson River. Lock 17 later replaced three locks of the original canal and measures 40.5 feet in height. Moss Island lies between the river and the Barge Canal, with the lock’s guillotine gate on its eastern side. That gate is a feature of the current Lock 17.

moments.title: Moss Island
moments.text: Circular potholes cut 40 to 50 feet into Moss Island, a rock island between the Mohawk River and the New York State Barge Canal. Its cliffs consist of metasyenite: rock first formed by cooling magma, then altered by heat and pressure without melting. Dwarf oaks cover the island, and glacial scratches remain visible in places. Canal construction made it an island, allowing boats to bypass the falls. It received National Natural Landmark designation in 1976. Beside the southeastern service road, a dry 19th-century Erie Canal lock survives alongside this geological record.
moments.notice: Circular potholes and patches of glacial scratches mark Moss Island’s rock.

moments.title: Nobleboro
moments.text: The South Branch West Canada Creek meets West Canada Creek at Nobleboro. Remains of a pulpwood boom and rossing mill lie along the creek, commemorated by a scenic overlook and kiosk. The hamlet’s earlier name, Noblesboro, came from its position at the boundary of a royal grant to Sir William Johnson.

moments.title: Speculator
moments.text: Speculator Mountain rises 2,966 feet just south of the village that took its name in 1896. Before that change, the settlement was Newton’s Corners, named through the post office Joel Newton secured with his store and hotel in 1864. Newton’s building burned in 1870. The post office reopened in another store, then moved to a new hotel on the old site; the name Speculator followed. The mountain remains visible from most of the village. Routes 8 and 30 meet here at the northeastern end of Lake Pleasant. The village incorporated in 1925, after the earlier change of name.
